text:
Yegor Sharangovich had a decent answer for his critics on Saturday. Two days after The Hockey Writers ran "Sharangovich Continuing to Give the Flames Nothing of Value," he set up Morgan Frost's opener in Los Angeles and then scored the winner with 1:14 left.

The season as a whole sits somewhere between the headline and the highlight. He has 10 points in 20 games, four of them goals on about five expected, so the finishing is roughly fair. Calgary takes 51% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him out there, almost five points better than without him, which is a quietly useful number on a team that usually loses that battle. He's also playing about 16 minutes a night, a real role.

Evolving-Hockey had him barely above replacement last season, so the skepticism isn't coming from nowhere. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking credits him with clean breakouts (71% of exits with possession). He's a fifth-round pick who has carved out a long NHL career with a heavy shot; what Calgary needs is more nights like Saturday.
